extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, potential petitioners, consumer advocates, regulated businesses, and practitioners/attorneys who would file or respond to FTC petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for submitting petitions for rulemaking (and related requests) to the Federal Trade Commission, and for how the Commission will handle, publish, and respond to those petitions to promote public participation and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on required information and helpful data
rubrics_metrics.description: More clarity for those seeking to file petitions related to rulemaking with regard to information that is required with submissions, as well as guidance on the data that can be helpful to the Commission in evaluation petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule changes aim to clarify what must be included in petition submissions and to offer guidance about the types of data that will assist the Commission in evaluating petitions (i.e., indicate what factual/data support strengthens a petition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish petitions in the Federal Register and solicit public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: A new requirement that the Commission publish all petitions for rulemaking that it receives in the Federal Register and solicit public comment about those petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All petitions will be made publicly available via the Federal Register and opened for public comment, creating an explicit opportunity for public input on each petition and increasing transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide petitioners with a specific point of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: A new requirement that the Commission provide petitioners with a specific point of contact in the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating a named or specific contact person/office for each petitioner is intended to improve accessibility and communication, especially for petitioners without counsel or institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a response to petitioners on decision to act or deny
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must provide a response to petitioners on its decision to either act on or deny the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike prior practice where there was no obligation to respond, the Commission will notify petitioners of its disposition (act/deny), thereby increasing procedural accountability and allowing petitioners to know the agency's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply new procedures to special exemption requests and industry guidance petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to formal rulemaking, the new changes will also apply to requests by certain parties for special exemption from FTC rules, as well as petitions related to industry guidance issued by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The broadened procedures are not limited to rulemaking petitions but cover discrete exemption requests and petitions concerning industry guidance, clarifying the scope of petition-processing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote public participation, accessibility, and guard against insularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The updates are designed to open the FTC’s regulatory processes to public input and scrutiny and to make the agency accessible 'even to those who lack well-heeled counsel or personal connections,' thereby promoting public participation and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching policy objective guiding the procedural changes: increase transparency, reduce agency insularity, and enhance institutional credibility by making petition processes accessible to laypersons and small stakeholders.
